extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers / Coursera learners interested in setting and description
extracted.subtask_description: An online course module sequence teaching how to ground fiction in concrete, credible, and evocative settings — covering sensory detail, research, and genre-specific approaches, with peer-review assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive setting
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'persuasive' setting is necessary in order to build mood, character, and even plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study masters (readings/videos) to see how setting persuades readers; Module 1 materials (e.g., 'The Power of Persuasion', 'Nothing Can Happen Nowhere') and the Slow-Motion Moment assignment provide practice in creating persuasive settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp, sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the physical world in sharp, sensory detail so readers can 'see' what you imagine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course emphasizes sensory specificity across modules; use concrete sensory cues rather than abstract summary. Module readings and examples demonstrate how detail anchors scenes; assignments ask you to render moments and rituals with rich sensory information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitamin-rich / significant detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Pack your fiction with 'vitamin-rich' detail — details that are funny, meaningful, and powerful (i.e., 'significant detail').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 ('What Is Significant Detail?') focuses on choosing details that carry thematic or emotional weight. Study both masters and student work to learn how small, well-chosen details deliver impact. Readings such as Wainaina, Moore, Wallace are given as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility through research (imaginative research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build credibility for your settings through research and 'imaginative research' when creating places unfamiliar to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 includes 'Three Phases of Research' and a 'Meditation Exercise' to guide research and internalization of setting. Use factual research to ground scenes and imaginative exercises to inhabit a place authentically; this supports believability without relying on stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common missteps in creating unfamiliar settings
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating settings both familiar and unfamiliar, take steps to avoid common missteps (e.g., reliance on cliché or inauthentic representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 warns about common pitfalls and directs learners to meditation and research exercises to prevent them. Peer-review assignment 'Strange Lands' gives practice and feedback focused on these missteps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of genre and scope (realist and non-realist applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting and description techniques should be adapted across realist and non-realist fiction and across literary genres; consider how genre shapes the use of setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 ('Realities') explicitly treats genre (including shop talks on Noir, historical fiction) and asks learners to reflect on their 'primal landscape.' Study genre-specific examples and visiting-writer talks to learn how conventions affect descriptive choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective movement through time and space
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle temporal and spatial transitions so scenes feel grounded and events occur in believable locations ('Moving Through Time and Space').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 contains content on moving through time and space and why 'Nothing Can Happen Nowhere.' Use description to orient readers and to support narrative pacing; mastering transitions is part of making settings persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooming into a Slow-Motion Moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to render a 'slow-motion moment' — focusing closely on a brief interval to reveal character, mood, and setting through concentrated detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 assignment 'Slow-Motion Moment' (peer-reviewed) practices this technique. The assignment timing (60 minutes) and supporting lectures encourage students to slow down perception and select vivid, telling specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting habitual ritual to reveal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Use habitual rituals and routines as descriptive material to reveal character and world ('Habitual Ritual').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2's assignment 'Habitual Ritual' and related readings encourage using everyday actions as a source of meaningful detail. Peer review (60 minutes) is part of the learning loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating believable Strange Lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Create unfamiliar or fantastical places ('Strange Lands') that feel credible to readers through detail, research, and imaginative grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3's long peer-reviewed assignment 'Strange Lands' (120 minutes) pairs research phases and meditation exercises to help writers render unfamiliar settings without implausibility or stereotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing about your 'primal landscape'
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and write from your own 'primal landscape' — the emotionally or experientially formative places that inform your descriptive voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 ('Primal Landscapes') asks learners to connect inner life and memory to descriptive practice. Assignments and examples encourage reflecting on how personal terrain shapes setting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer feedback aligned with specialization expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and receive peer feedback according to the Specialization's feedback expectations (guidance provided in course materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 includes 'Feedback Expectations for the Specialization' (video). Each module includes peer-review assignments (with specified time expectations) that require learners to critique peers' use of detail, credibility, and setting — follow the course's feedback rubric/videos when reviewing.
